Gas vs. a year ago

lines.text: Gas costs $1.13 a gallon more than a year ago.
lines.say: Gas costs a dollar thirteen a gallon more than a year ago.

lines.text: AAA's national average was $3.04 this time last year. This morning it's $4.17.
lines.say: AAA's national average was three dollars and four cents this time last year. This morning, it's four seventeen.

lines.text: Government data say October averaged $4.31, the highest October since at least 1990.
lines.say: Government data say October averaged four thirty-one, the highest October since at least 1990.

lines.text: Even 2022, the year everyone complained about gas, was $3.82 in October.
lines.say: Even 2022, the year everyone complained about gas, was three eighty-two in October.

lines.text: AAA says the culprit is crude oil, still above $100 a barrel.
lines.say: AAA says the culprit is crude oil, which is still above a hundred dollars a barrel.

lines.text: Overnight, oil futures slipped on hopes for Iran talks mediated by Qatar.
lines.say: Overnight, oil futures slipped on hopes for Iran talks mediated by Qatar.

lines.text: Diesel hurts more: $6.29, up from $3.68. That's the fuel trucks use to move your groceries.

post.title: Gas costs $1.13 more a gallon than a year ago
post.ig:
A gallon of gas costs $1.13 more than a year ago.
AAA national average: $4.17 today (Nov 2) vs $3.04 a year ago, even after falling about 23 cents in a month.
October averaged $4.31 (EIA), the highest October since at least 1990. October 2022 was $3.82.
Diesel: $6.29 vs $3.68 a year ago. AAA says crude above $100 a barrel is the culprit.
Our math: a 15-gallon fill-up costs $17 more than last year.
Sources: AAA (Nov 2, 2026); U.S. Energy Information Administration; Newsquawk (Nov 2).
News and education, not financial advice.
